For those new to the game or to how the economy works: simple rules and more leeway; advanced options open up little by little and each screen is explained the first time. One life: 10–15 min.
Calibrated with real data and simple rules: automatic pay and expenses, wars with one battle a year, everything visible. One life: 10–15 min.
All mechanics: taxes, inflation, loans, month-by-month wars, diseases, congress and trials. One life: 30–60 min.

Keeping money in a bank protects it and earns interest (the deposit rate). Small banks pay more because they fail more often; if one fails, your country’s deposit insurance returns up to a cap per bank. Here you also take out loans: the interest depends on your credit history.

A share is a small piece of a company. If the company does well, the price rises and some pay dividends; if it does badly, you can lose. Buying companies from different sectors (diversifying) reduces the damage when a single one falls.

A company sells every month and pays for supplies, wages, rent, taxes and debts; what is left is the profit, and what it pays out reaches your money. Starting small and reinvesting is safer than borrowing to grow fast.

Services you pay for every month: protection, health, help at home. They improve your life or lower risks (for example, kidnapping when you have a lot of money), but they are a fixed cost: hire them when your income can carry them.
Your money for the year: gross income minus living costs (and, in Realistic, taxes and loan payments) gives your net. If the net is negative, you spend more than you earn and your savings shrink.

Here you decide how to spend your time. Each activity costs time or money and moves your stats: studying raises intelligence; the gym, health; family, happiness. Those stats decide which doors open later.

How you earn a living. A job pays from day one; university takes years but opens better-paid jobs; the careers to power (politics, army, business) lead to ruling. Wages come from your country’s real average wage.
What you own: house, cars and other assets. Your net worth is everything you own (cash, accounts, investments and assets) minus what you owe.
Your relationships: family, partner, friends and contacts. They cool off if you don’t give them time; contacts open jobs and deals for you.
Your ambition is the goal you chose for this life: here you see how far you have to go and the achievements you already have.
Each country with real 2026 data: population, economy, army and relations with other countries. What happens in yours (wars, crises, wages) affects you too.
🩺 Your health is low: see a doctor or go to the gym.
🌴 Your happiness is low: spend time with your family or take a vacation.
📚 Study: intelligence raises your grades and opens better careers.
💼 Find a job or go to university: it is your first source of income.
📉 You spend more than you earn: look for a better-paid job or get more training.
🏦 You have idle cash: in a bank account it earns interest.
📈 Diversify: put part of your savings into an investment fund.
🏪 You could start a business now: a company can give you more than a salary.
The general rise in prices over a year. With 5 % inflation, what cost $100 costs $105: if your pay does not rise as much, you can buy less.
Gross domestic product: the value of everything a country produces in a year. It measures the size of its economy.
GDP divided by the population. It is used to compare how rich each country is on average.
The typical annual pay of a worker in the country. The game uses it as the basis for wages and prices.
The price of money over time, in % per year: what the bank pays you to keep your money or charges you to lend it.
A government guarantee: if your bank fails, it returns your deposits up to a cap per bank. Anything above the cap can be lost.
A small piece of a company that is bought and sold on the stock exchange. Its price rises or falls with what is expected of the company.
The part of its profits a company pays out to its shareholders.
Spreading your money across several different investments so that a fall in one does not hurt you too much.
What is left of sales after paying all costs. If it is negative, the company loses money.
Everything you own (cash, accounts, investments and assets) minus everything you owe.
A rating of how reliable you are at paying back. With a good history, you can borrow more at lower interest.
What you pay the government on your income and purchases. It pays for schools, hospitals, the army and public works.
When a company or bank cannot pay what it owes and closes or is taken over.
